title: Sparkle: A Robust and Versatile Representation for Point Cloud-based Human Motion Capture
claim: A three-stage modular system turns noisy, diverse sensor inputs into a structured intermediate representation and then into final body-model output.
layout: 4 panels, left-to-right; input gallery then three module boxes with dashed skip arrows
description: A wide figure in four columns, read left to right. The left column is a dashed gallery of input point clouds: LiDAR with occlusion, object noise and environment noise, depth-camera humans, close interaction, and multi-view setups. Three rounded teal-gray panels follow, each titled with a module name. The first, the Point-aligned Skeleton Tracker, runs a PointNet-GRU, then joint and root/head/foot point-aligned optimization, with symbols such as J_init, L_j and T_init. The second, the Skeleton-guided Anchor Estimator, shows a ground-truth joint-to-anchor correspondence and a kinematic-aware optimizer, with colored token grids F_joint and F_anchor. The third, the Sparkle-based SMPL Solver, shows Sparkle and Template skeletons, feature interaction between F_sparkle and F_pose, and blue SMPL meshes as output. Dashed gray arrows link the stages. The eye goes first to the colorful skeleton and token visuals.
caption: The pipeline of SparkleMotion. It can take point clouds of diverse patterns as input in different challenge scenarios, as shown on the left. SparkleMotion consists of three primary modules, the Point-aligned Skeleton Tracker, and Skeleton-guided Anchor Estimator construct the Sparkle Representation, and the Sparkle-based SMPL Solver for motion reconstruction.
abstract: Point cloud-based motion capture leverages rich spatial geometry and privacy-preserving sensing, but learning robust representations from noisy, unstructured point clouds remains challenging. Existing approaches face a struggle trade-off between point-based methods (geometrically detailed but noisy) and skeleton-based ones (robust but oversimplified). We address the fundamental challenge: how to construct an effective representation for human motion capture that can balance expressiveness and robustness. In this paper, we propose Sparkle, a structured representation unifying skeletal joints and surface anchors with explicit kinematic-geometric factorization. Our framework, SparkleMotion, learns this representation through hierarchical modules embedding geometric continuity and kinematic constraints. By explicitly disentangling internal kinematic structure from external surface geometry, SparkleMotion achieves state-of-the-art performance not only in accuracy but crucially in robustness and generalization under severe domain shifts, noise, and occlusion. Extensive experiments demonstrate our superiority across diverse sensor types and challenging real-world scenarios.
